title: South Dakota Codified Laws Chapter 3-6C - State Employment General Provisions
verified_how: fetched https://sdlegislature.gov/api/Statutes/Statute/3-6C: Type 'Chapter', CatchLine 'STATE EMPLOYMENT GENERAL PROVISIONS', Repealed false. Its section catchlines include 'Vacation leave--Accrual and accumulation--Advanced leave', 'Sick leave--Accrual and accumulation--Medical certificate--Vacation leave used for sickness--Personal emergency leave', 'Paid family leave', 'Holiday benefit eligibility', 'Payment for accrued unused sick leave on termination of employment' and 'Donation of accrued vested leave to another employee'. Confirmed on the Title 3 index (https://sdlegislature.gov/api/Statutes/Statute/3) as chapter row '06C State Employment General Provisions', with the predecessor ch. 3-6 marked '[Repealed And Transferred]' and ch. 3-6A marked '[Repealed]'. Currency: code effective date 2026-09-03.
notes: IMPORTANT SCOPE LIMIT: this binds the State as an employer, not private employers. South Dakota has no private-sector annual-leave, sick-leave, paid-family-leave or holiday-pay entitlement statute; private-sector family and medical leave is federal (FMLA, 29 U.S.C. ch. 28). Legal holidays themselves are designated by SDCL ch. 1-5 (Time and Dates), sec. 1-5-1 'Holidays enumerated', verified in force on the register's API, but that chapter designates days and validates transactions rather than creating any pay entitlement. A human should decide whether a state-employee-only statute is the right fit for this topic.
